caption_hook: 🚴 A cyclist rode the old Pony Express mail route across America and beat the riders' 1861 record by nearly 20 hours + 3 more wins 👇
question: Horse 🐎 or bike 🚴: which would you pick for 1,966 miles?
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves a challenge

first_comment: Bonus: the 1861 riders used about 197 horses to rush Abraham Lincoln's inaugural address west. Lachlan carried real letters from the public too. Who would you send a letter to? ✉️

stories.headline: A cyclist beat a 165-year-old Pony Express record
stories.summary: Lachlan Morton rode the 1,966-mile route from St. Joseph, Missouri, to Sacramento in 6 days, 21 hours and 15 minutes, swapping between 3 bikes through mud, sand, headwinds and the Sierra Nevada.
stories.why: He wanted to feel what the young mail riders went through crossing the West in 1861.

stories.headline: AI helped find 70 new natural telescopes in space
stories.summary: An AI scanned a map of nearly 4 billion objects for gravitational lenses, where a galaxy's gravity magnifies one behind it. A telescope in Chile then confirmed 70 of 76 candidates.
stories.why: Each lens lets astronomers see distant galaxies and map invisible dark matter.

stories.headline: India added 2 lakes and now protects 103 world-class wetlands
stories.summary: Sukhna Lake in Chandigarh, at the foot of the Himalayas, and Sauj Jheel in Uttar Pradesh joined the global Ramsar list of protected wetlands, taking India's total to 103.
stories.why: Wetlands store water, prevent floods and shelter migrating birds.

stories.headline: Egypt cut hepatitis C from 10% to under 0.4%, and kept it there
stories.summary: A national campaign screened 60 million+ people and treated 4.5 million+ with locally made medicine. Egypt is now the 1st country the WHO has confirmed kept its 'gold tier' status.
stories.why: A disease that once touched 1 in 10 people is now rare, and the gains are holding.

fun_fact: The Pony Express ran for only 18 months before the telegraph made it obsolete in 1861.
